title: Hodgkin Lymphoma
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: DRAFT decision support authored from standard oncology references (NCCN / DeVita / Harrison) - the physician decides. Pathway branches by histology (classical HL vs NLPHL vs pediatric / adolescent vs relapsed / refractory), then workup -> Ann Arbor / Lugano staging and favorable-vs-unfavorable or IPS risk -> stage- and regimen-directed frontline therapy (ABVD vs BV-AVD vs escalated BEACOPP) with interim-PET (Deauville) response adaptation, then an end-of-treatment restaging response step that separates complete metabolic response from residual / refractory disease -> survivorship surveillance -> relapse detection -> a line-of-therapy relapsed / refractory cascade (salvage + autologous transplant, transplant-ineligible sequential novel agents, and multiply-relapsed / post-transplant checkpoint / allogeneic / trial options). Every major treatment arm is refined by a response or line-of-therapy decision before a recommendation. End nodes reference an existing StewardMD Standard Protocol only where one clinically fits (pediatric ABVE-PC; transformed NLPHL treated as aggressive B-cell lymphoma with R-CHOP); adult HL regimens (ABVD / BV-AVD / BEACOPP / ICE / DHAP / brentuximab / checkpoint salvage) have no dedicated dose protocol in the library and are shown as described guidance without invented doses. Structural content is standard oncology; no proprietary guideline text is reproduced. DRAFT - not clinically activated.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with standard oncology references (NCCN / DeVita / Harrison), Hodgkin Lymphoma. Pediatric and transformed-histology regimen options reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols; the dose engine computes patient doses. Adult HL regimens without a dose protocol are shown as checklist guidance with no invented dose.

a.text: Interim FDG-PET after 2 cycles is scored on the 5-point Deauville scale; Deauville 1-3 is treated as a negative (adequate) metabolic response and Deauville 4-5 as positive (inadequate) response. End-of-treatment PET is interpreted the same way to define complete metabolic response.

b.text: Bleomycin carries a risk of cumulative pulmonary toxicity; response-adapted omission after a negative interim PET (continuing as AVD) reduces lung exposure without loss of disease control in the settings where it has been studied.

c.text: Discuss fertility preservation before gonadotoxic chemotherapy or pelvic radiation, and counsel on long-term risks (second malignancy, cardiac, thyroid, pulmonary) that drive lifelong survivorship follow-up.

d.text: Escalated BEACOPP achieves high disease control at the cost of greater acute toxicity, infertility, and second-malignancy risk; reserve for selected fit, higher-risk younger patients and weigh explicitly against ABVD / BV-AVD.

e.text: For relapsed / refractory classical HL, brentuximab vedotin (CD30-directed) and PD-1 checkpoint inhibitors (nivolumab, pembrolizumab) are active as salvage and post-transplant maintenance; a persistently PET-positive site should be re-biopsied to confirm active disease before it is treated as refractory.

nodes.title: Hodgkin lymphoma: histology / presentation
nodes.description: Management branches first by histologic subtype and treatment context. Choose the applicable category.
bullets: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL) - newly diagnosed

nodes.name: cHL workup
nodes.title: Classical HL: workup and staging studies
nodes.description: Confirm the diagnosis and complete pre-treatment staging and organ-function baselines.
bullets: Excisional / core-needle nodal biopsy with hematopathology review confirming CD30-positive Reed-Sternberg cells
History and physical: assess B symptoms (fever, drenching night sweats, weight loss), pruritus, alcohol-induced pain, ECOG performance status
Whole-body FDG-PET/CT for staging (Ann Arbor with Lugano modifications); mark bulky disease for later radiation planning
CBC, ESR, LDH, comprehensive metabolic panel, albumin; HIV and hepatitis B/C serologies
Baseline echocardiogram / MUGA before anthracycline and pulmonary function tests before bleomycin
Fertility counseling and preservation before gonadotoxic therapy; pregnancy test where applicable

nodes.name: cHL stage group
nodes.title: Classical HL: Ann Arbor stage group
nodes.description: Split into limited-stage (I-II) and advanced-stage (III-IV) disease; limited stage is further stratified by favorable vs unfavorable risk factors.

tables.title: Ann Arbor / Lugano stage (simplified)
rows: Single nodal region or single extranodal site
Two or more nodal regions, same side of the diaphragm
Nodal regions on both sides of the diaphragm

nodes.name: Early risk group
nodes.title: Limited-stage cHL: favorable vs unfavorable
nodes.description: Any listed adverse factor moves early-stage disease from favorable to unfavorable and intensifies therapy.

tables.title: Common unfavorable factors in early-stage cHL

nodes.name: Early favorable interim PET
nodes.title: Early favorable cHL: interim PET after ABVD x2
nodes.description: Start ABVD; reassess with interim FDG-PET after 2 cycles and adapt by Deauville response.
nodes.path: Hodgkin / cHL / Early favorable / Interim PET
bullets: Give ABVD x2 cycles, then interim FDG-PET scored by Deauville
Negative interim PET (Deauville 1-3) supports abbreviating therapy and de-escalation
Positive interim PET (Deauville 4-5) prompts continued / intensified chemotherapy plus radiation

nodes.name: Early fav PET-neg EOT
nodes.title: Early favorable, interim PET-negative: complete therapy, then end-of-treatment PET
nodes.description: Complete abbreviated therapy after a negative interim scan, then restage with end-of-treatment PET and separate complete metabolic response from residual disease.
nodes.path: Hodgkin / cHL / Early favorable / PET-neg / EOT
bullets: Option A (combined-modality): complete a short ABVD course (total ~2-4 cycles) followed by involved-site radiation (ISRT)
Option B (chemotherapy-alone): extend ABVD to ~3-4 cycles to spare radiation in selected non-bulky patients
Consider dropping bleomycin in later cycles after a negative interim PET to reduce pulmonary toxicity
Restage with end-of-treatment FDG-PET (Deauville) before declaring remission

nodes.name: Early fav CR
nodes.title: Early favorable cHL in complete metabolic response
nodes.description: Treatment complete with a negative end-of-treatment PET; move to survivorship surveillance.
bullets: No further anti-lymphoma therapy for a documented complete metabolic response
Confirm cumulative anthracycline dose and bleomycin exposure are recorded for late-effect follow-up
Reinforce late-effect and fertility counseling
Then survivorship surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Early fav residual
nodes.title: Early favorable cHL with residual PET-positive disease
nodes.description: A persistently PET-positive site after planned therapy needs confirmation and consolidation or salvage.
bullets: Re-biopsy the residual PET-positive site to confirm active Hodgkin lymphoma before escalating
Involved-site radiation (ISRT) to a confirmed localized residual site if not already given
If biopsy confirms refractory disease, enter the relapsed / refractory pathway for salvage +/- transplant
Then survivorship surveillance if the residual finding resolves
nodes.linkLabel: If biopsy-confirmed refractory: go to the relapsed / refractory pathway

nodes.name: Early fav PET-pos
nodes.title: Early favorable, interim PET-positive: escalate + ISRT
nodes.description: An inadequate interim response upgrades therapy to full-intensity chemotherapy plus radiation.
bullets: Continue full-intensity chemotherapy (complete ABVD, or escalate to escalated BEACOPP x2 in fit patients)
Add involved-site radiation (ISRT) to residual / bulky sites
Re-biopsy a persistently PET-positive site to exclude refractory disease before declaring failure
If refractory, route to the relapsed / refractory pathway; otherwise proceed to surveillance
Then survivorship surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Early unfavorable interim PET
nodes.title: Early unfavorable cHL: interim PET after ABVD x2
nodes.description: Start ABVD; reassess with interim FDG-PET after 2 cycles. Unfavorable disease generally receives more cycles and radiation to bulk.
nodes.path: Hodgkin / cHL / Early unfavorable / Interim PET

nodes.name: Early unfav PET-neg
nodes.title: Early unfavorable, interim PET-negative: combined-modality
nodes.description: Complete chemotherapy with involved-site radiation, then surveillance.
bullets: Complete ABVD (typically ~4 cycles total) followed by involved-site radiation (ISRT), especially to bulky sites
Chemotherapy-alone (extending ABVD, omitting radiation) is an option in selected non-bulky patients to reduce late radiation risk
Consider dropping bleomycin after a negative interim PET to limit pulmonary toxicity
End-of-treatment PET to confirm complete metabolic response
Then survivorship surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Early unfav PET-pos escalate
nodes.title: Early unfavorable, interim PET-positive: intensify, then end-of-treatment PET
nodes.description: Escalate systemic therapy and consolidate with radiation, then restage to separate complete response from refractory disease.
nodes.path: Hodgkin / cHL / Early unfavorable / PET-pos / EOT
bullets: Escalate systemic therapy (e.g. switch to escalated BEACOPP in fit patients) and add involved-site radiation (ISRT)
Re-biopsy a persistently PET-positive site to confirm active disease before treating as refractory
Restage with end-of-treatment FDG-PET (Deauville) to define the outcome

nodes.name: Early unfav escalate CR
nodes.title: Early unfavorable cHL: complete response after escalation
nodes.description: Complete metabolic response after intensified therapy; move to surveillance.
nodes.path: Hodgkin / cHL / Early unfavorable / Escalated / CR
bullets: No further anti-lymphoma therapy for a documented complete metabolic response
Record cumulative anthracycline / alkylator exposure for late-effect follow-up
Reinforce second-malignancy and cardiac screening given escalated therapy
Then survivorship surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Early unfav refractory
nodes.title: Early unfavorable cHL: primary refractory
nodes.description: Biopsy-proven disease after intensified frontline therapy is primary refractory and enters the salvage pathway.
bullets: Confirm active disease by biopsy of a PET-positive site
Treat as primary refractory classical HL: enter the relapsed / refractory salvage pathway
Salvage aims for a chemosensitive PET-negative response before high-dose therapy and autologous transplant
Consider brentuximab- or checkpoint-based salvage in this high-risk setting
nodes.linkLabel: Go to the relapsed / refractory salvage pathway

nodes.name: Advanced IPS
nodes.title: Advanced cHL: International Prognostic Score (IPS)
nodes.description: The IPS counts adverse factors and informs regimen intensity for advanced-stage disease; it does not by itself mandate a specific drug.

nodes.name: Advanced regimen
nodes.title: Advanced cHL: frontline regimen choice
nodes.description: Select the first-line backbone; ABVD is PET-adapted, BV-AVD front-loads brentuximab vedotin, and escalated BEACOPP is reserved for selected higher-risk fit younger patients.

nodes.name: Advanced ABVD interim PET
nodes.title: Advanced cHL on ABVD: interim PET after 2 cycles
nodes.description: Adapt ABVD by interim FDG-PET (Deauville) after 2 cycles - de-escalate on a negative scan, escalate on a positive scan.
nodes.path: Hodgkin / cHL / Advanced / ABVD / Interim PET

nodes.name: Advanced ABVD PET-neg EOT
nodes.title: Advanced cHL, ABVD interim PET-negative: drop bleomycin, then end-of-treatment PET
nodes.description: Continue AVD (bleomycin omitted) to complete ~6 cycles, then restage to separate complete response from residual disease.
nodes.path: Hodgkin / cHL / Advanced / ABVD / PET-neg / EOT
bullets: Omit bleomycin and continue AVD to complete ~6 cycles total
Radiation is generally not added for advanced-stage disease in complete metabolic response
End-of-treatment FDG-PET (Deauville) defines the outcome

nodes.name: Advanced ABVD CR
nodes.title: Advanced cHL, ABVD/AVD complete metabolic response
nodes.description: Full course completed with a negative end-of-treatment PET.
bullets: No further anti-lymphoma therapy or consolidative radiation for advanced-stage disease in complete metabolic response
Record cumulative doxorubicin dose for cardiac late-effect follow-up
Reinforce fertility and second-malignancy counseling
Then survivorship surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Advanced ABVD residual
nodes.title: Advanced cHL, ABVD/AVD residual PET-positive disease
nodes.description: A residual PET-positive site after full chemotherapy needs biopsy and consolidation or salvage.
bullets: Re-biopsy the residual PET-positive site to confirm active Hodgkin lymphoma
Involved-site radiation to a confirmed localized residual site
If biopsy confirms refractory disease, enter the relapsed / refractory salvage pathway
Then survivorship surveillance if the residual finding resolves
nodes.linkLabel: If biopsy-confirmed refractory: go to the salvage pathway

nodes.name: Advanced ABVD PET-pos escalate
nodes.title: Advanced cHL, ABVD interim PET-positive: escalate, then end-of-treatment PET
nodes.description: Switch to a more intensive regimen for an inadequate interim response, then restage to define the outcome.
nodes.path: Hodgkin / cHL / Advanced / ABVD / PET-pos / EOT
bullets: Escalate to escalated BEACOPP (in fit patients) for the remaining cycles
Consider radiation to residual bulky / focally PET-positive sites
Re-biopsy persistent PET positivity to confirm active disease before treating as refractory
Restage with end-of-treatment FDG-PET (Deauville)

nodes.name: Advanced ABVD escalate CR
nodes.title: Advanced cHL: complete response after escalation
nodes.description: Complete metabolic response after switching to intensified therapy for a positive interim PET.
nodes.path: Hodgkin / cHL / Advanced / ABVD / Escalated / CR
bullets: No further anti-lymphoma therapy for a documented complete metabolic response
Consolidative radiation only to a residual bulky site, per institutional practice
Record cumulative anthracycline / alkylator exposure for late-effect follow-up
Then survivorship surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Advanced ABVD refractory
nodes.title: Advanced cHL: primary refractory after escalation
nodes.description: Biopsy-proven disease after intensified frontline therapy enters the salvage pathway.
bullets: Confirm active disease by biopsy of a PET-positive site
Treat as primary refractory classical HL: enter the relapsed / refractory salvage pathway
Salvage aims for a chemosensitive PET-negative response before high-dose therapy and autologous transplant
Brentuximab- or checkpoint-based salvage is preferred in this high-risk setting
nodes.linkLabel: Go to the relapsed / refractory salvage pathway

nodes.name: Advanced BV-AVD EOT
nodes.title: Advanced cHL: BV-AVD (brentuximab vedotin + AVD), then end-of-treatment PET
nodes.description: Brentuximab vedotin replaces bleomycin in the AVD backbone as a first-line option; restage after ~6 cycles.
bullets: Brentuximab vedotin + doxorubicin, vinblastine, dacarbazine (A+AVD) for ~6 cycles
Give primary G-CSF prophylaxis (higher neutropenia risk) and monitor for peripheral neuropathy
No dedicated adult HL dose protocol exists in StewardMD yet - dosing is per standard references; guidance only
End-of-treatment FDG-PET (Deauville) defines the outcome

nodes.name: Advanced BV-AVD CR
nodes.title: Advanced cHL, BV-AVD complete metabolic response
nodes.description: Full BV-AVD course completed with a negative end-of-treatment PET.
bullets: No further anti-lymphoma therapy for a documented complete metabolic response
Continue peripheral-neuropathy monitoring and taper as needed after brentuximab
Record cumulative anthracycline dose for cardiac late-effect follow-up
Then survivorship surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Advanced BV-AVD residual
nodes.title: Advanced cHL, BV-AVD residual / refractory disease
nodes.description: A residual PET-positive site after BV-AVD needs biopsy and salvage.
bullets: Re-biopsy the residual PET-positive site to confirm active disease
Involved-site radiation to a confirmed localized residual site
If refractory, enter the relapsed / refractory salvage pathway; checkpoint-based salvage is reasonable after brentuximab exposure
Then survivorship surveillance if the residual finding resolves
nodes.linkLabel: If biopsy-confirmed refractory: go to the salvage pathway

nodes.name: Advanced BEACOPP EOT
nodes.title: Advanced cHL: escalated BEACOPP, PET-adapted cycles, then end-of-treatment PET
nodes.description: Intensive multi-agent regimen for selected fit, higher-risk younger patients; number of cycles is PET-adapted, then restage.
bullets: Escalated BEACOPP with PET-adapted cycle number; high disease control but greater acute toxicity
Mandatory G-CSF support; counsel on infertility and second-malignancy risk before starting
No dedicated adult HL dose protocol exists in StewardMD yet - dosing is per standard references; guidance only
End-of-treatment FDG-PET (Deauville) defines the outcome

nodes.name: Advanced BEACOPP CR
nodes.title: Advanced cHL, escalated BEACOPP complete response
nodes.description: Complete metabolic response after escalated BEACOPP.
bullets: No further anti-lymphoma therapy for a documented complete metabolic response
Consolidative radiation only to a residual bulky site, per institutional practice
Prioritize second-malignancy, cardiac, and fertility late-effect screening after intensive therapy
Then survivorship surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Advanced BEACOPP residual
nodes.title: Advanced cHL, escalated BEACOPP residual disease
nodes.description: A residual PET-positive site after escalated BEACOPP needs biopsy, radiation, or salvage.
bullets: Re-biopsy the residual PET-positive site to confirm active disease
Involved-site radiation to a confirmed localized residual site
If refractory after intensive frontline therapy, enter the salvage pathway (brentuximab / checkpoint-based salvage)
Then survivorship surveillance if the residual finding resolves
nodes.linkLabel: If biopsy-confirmed refractory: go to the salvage pathway

nodes.name: Surveillance
nodes.title: Survivorship surveillance / follow-up
nodes.description: Follow-up after curative-intent therapy, emphasizing relapse detection and late-effect screening. Choose the follow-up status.
bullets: History and physical every 3-6 months for 1-2 years, then lengthening intervals; labs (CBC, ESR if elevated at baseline, TSH if neck irradiated)
Avoid routine surveillance PET in asymptomatic remission (false positives); image to evaluate new symptoms or findings
Screen for late effects: cardiac, thyroid, pulmonary, and second malignancies (including breast screening after chest radiation)
Reinforce vaccination and infection precautions; counsel on fertility and psychosocial survivorship needs

nodes.name: Continued remission
nodes.title: Continued remission: long-term survivorship
nodes.description: Sustained remission on long-term survivorship follow-up.
bullets: Continue risk-based late-effect screening (cardiac, thyroid, pulmonary, second malignancy) for life
Breast MRI / mammography screening starting ~8-10 years after chest radiation (or by age 30) for women irradiated when young
Cardiovascular risk-factor management and smoking cessation to limit anthracycline / radiation cardiac risk
Address fertility, bone health, and psychosocial survivorship needs at each visit

nodes.name: Relapse candidacy
nodes.title: Relapsed / refractory cHL: transplant candidacy
nodes.description: Biopsy-confirm relapse and restage. Transplant-eligible patients receive salvage chemotherapy to a chemosensitive response, then high-dose therapy and autologous stem-cell transplant.
bullets: Confirm relapse histologically and restage with FDG-PET/CT
Assess transplant eligibility (age, comorbidity, prior therapy, chemosensitivity)
Timing since frontline (primary refractory, early < 12-month relapse, late relapse) informs prognosis and salvage choice

nodes.name: Salvage response
nodes.title: Salvage chemotherapy: pre-transplant PET response
nodes.description: Second-line chemotherapy aims for a chemosensitive PET-negative response; the depth of response before high-dose therapy drives outcome and next steps.
bullets: Second-line chemotherapy: platinum-based ICE / DHAP, or brentuximab-based or checkpoint-based salvage
Restage with FDG-PET before high-dose therapy; a PET-negative (chemosensitive) response predicts better transplant outcome
No dedicated adult HL salvage dose protocol exists in StewardMD yet - dosing is per standard references; guidance only

nodes.name: Salvage + ASCT
nodes.title: High-dose therapy + autologous transplant (chemosensitive relapse)
nodes.description: High-dose chemotherapy with autologous stem-cell rescue for chemosensitive relapse, with risk-adapted brentuximab maintenance.
bullets: High-dose chemotherapy + autologous stem-cell transplant (ASCT) for chemosensitive (PET-negative) disease
Brentuximab vedotin maintenance for high-risk features (primary refractory, relapse < 12 months, extranodal relapse)
No dedicated adult HL transplant-conditioning dose protocol exists in StewardMD yet - dosing is per standard references; guidance only
Post-transplant surveillance for relapse and late effects

nodes.name: Second salvage
nodes.title: Inadequate salvage response: switch salvage before transplant
nodes.description: A PET-positive response to first salvage prompts a non-cross-resistant second salvage to achieve chemosensitivity before transplant.
bullets: Switch to a non-cross-resistant salvage (e.g. checkpoint- or brentuximab-based if not already used, or an alternate platinum regimen)
Aim to convert to a PET-negative response, then proceed to autologous transplant
Consider allogeneic transplant in selected fit patients who reach a chemosensitive response but have very high-risk disease
No dedicated adult HL salvage dose protocol exists in StewardMD yet - dosing is per standard references; guidance only

nodes.name: Non-transplant line
nodes.title: Transplant-ineligible relapse: sequential line of therapy
nodes.description: For patients not eligible for transplant, sequence CD30- and checkpoint-directed agents by line, reserving palliative measures for later lines.
bullets: Sequential single agents are preferred over intensive chemotherapy in transplant-ineligible patients
Choose the first novel agent by prior exposure and comorbidity
Reassess response before each change of therapy

nodes.name: R/R brentuximab
nodes.title: Transplant-ineligible relapse: brentuximab vedotin
nodes.description: CD30-directed antibody-drug conjugate as a first novel-agent line.
bullets: Brentuximab vedotin (CD30-directed) as a single agent for CD30-positive relapse
Monitor for peripheral neuropathy and neutropenia; dose-modify per tolerance
Reassess response with imaging; switch to a checkpoint inhibitor on progression
No dedicated adult HL dose protocol exists in StewardMD yet - dosing is per standard references; guidance only

nodes.name: R/R checkpoint
nodes.title: Transplant-ineligible relapse: PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor
nodes.description: PD-1 blockade after progression on a prior novel agent.
bullets: PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor (nivolumab or pembrolizumab), highly active in classical HL
Consider brentuximab + nivolumab combinations in selected patients
Monitor for immune-related adverse events; use standard immunotherapy toxicity management
No dedicated adult HL dose protocol exists in StewardMD yet - dosing is per standard references; guidance only

nodes.name: R/R palliative
nodes.title: Transplant-ineligible relapse: palliative therapy
nodes.description: Palliative systemic or local therapy and best supportive care in later lines.
bullets: Palliative single-agent chemotherapy (e.g. gemcitabine-based) or low-dose involved-site radiation for local symptom control
Best supportive care, symptom management, and early palliative-care involvement
Clinical-trial referral where appropriate
No dedicated adult HL dose protocol exists in StewardMD yet - dosing is per standard references; guidance only

nodes.name: Multiply relapsed
nodes.title: Multiply relapsed / post-ASCT: next-line strategy
nodes.description: After prior transplant, prioritize checkpoint blockade, then consider allogeneic transplant or clinical-trial / cellular therapy.
bullets: Checkpoint blockade (with or without brentuximab) is the usual next step after ASCT
Allogeneic transplant is considered in selected fit patients with a chemosensitive response
Clinical trials of cellular / novel agents are appropriate throughout

nodes.name: Multiply checkpoint
nodes.title: Multiply relapsed: checkpoint inhibitor
nodes.description: PD-1 blockade, alone or combined with brentuximab, after prior transplant.
bullets: PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor (nivolumab or pembrolizumab), with or without brentuximab vedotin
Durable responses can bridge selected patients to allogeneic transplant
Monitor for immune-related adverse events; note increased GVHD risk if allo-transplant follows checkpoint therapy
No dedicated adult HL dose protocol exists in StewardMD yet - dosing is per standard references; guidance only

nodes.name: Multiply allo
nodes.title: Multiply relapsed: allogeneic transplant
nodes.description: Reduced-intensity allogeneic transplant for selected fit patients in a chemosensitive response.
bullets: Reduced-intensity-conditioning allogeneic stem-cell transplant for fit patients with a chemosensitive response after prior ASCT
Weigh graft-versus-lymphoma benefit against transplant-related mortality and chronic GVHD
Prior checkpoint-inhibitor exposure raises GVHD risk - plan timing and prophylaxis accordingly
No dedicated adult HL transplant-conditioning dose protocol exists in StewardMD yet - dosing is per standard references; guidance only

nodes.name: Multiply trial
nodes.title: Multiply relapsed: clinical trial / cellular therapy
nodes.description: Investigational and cellular approaches for chemorefractory multiply-relapsed disease.
bullets: Refer to clinical trials of novel agents or cellular therapy (e.g. CD30-directed cellular products under investigation)
Continue palliative and supportive care in parallel
Reassess goals of care and involve palliative care early in the refractory setting
No dedicated adult HL dose protocol exists in StewardMD yet - dosing is per standard references; guidance only

nodes.name: NLPHL workup
nodes.title: NLPHL: workup
nodes.description: NLPHL is CD20-positive and CD30/CD15-negative, behaves more indolently, and is managed differently from classical HL.
bullets: Excisional biopsy with immunohistochemistry (CD20+, CD45+, CD30-, CD15-) confirming NLPHL; assess for a variant / transformed pattern
FDG-PET/CT staging; note that transformation to aggressive B-cell lymphoma occurs in a minority
Baseline labs (CBC, LDH, metabolic panel); viral serologies before anti-CD20 therapy
Fertility counseling if chemotherapy is planned

nodes.name: NLPHL stage
nodes.title: NLPHL: stage / pattern
nodes.description: Treatment intensity is guided by stage and by whether a variant / transformed histology is present.

nodes.name: NLPHL early
nodes.title: Early-stage NLPHL: local therapy, then response
nodes.description: Localized NLPHL is often cured with radiation alone; observation after complete excision is reasonable in select cases. Reassess response before surveillance.
bullets: Involved-site radiation (ISRT) alone for early-stage disease
Observation after complete surgical excision is an option for a single fully resected node
Rituximab (anti-CD20) may be added or substituted in selected patients
Restage after local therapy to confirm response

nodes.name: NLPHL early CR
nodes.title: Early NLPHL in complete response
nodes.description: Localized NLPHL controlled by local therapy; move to surveillance.
bullets: No further therapy after a complete response to radiation or excision
NLPHL can relapse late - maintain long-term follow-up and re-biopsy any relapse to exclude transformation
Then survivorship surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: NLPHL early persistent
nodes.title: Early NLPHL with persistent / progressive disease
nodes.description: Persistent disease after local therapy escalates to systemic anti-CD20-based therapy.
bullets: Re-biopsy to confirm persistent NLPHL and exclude transformation to aggressive B-cell lymphoma
Escalate to rituximab-based systemic therapy (see advanced NLPHL)
Additional involved-site radiation to a localized persistent site if not previously given
Then survivorship surveillance if disease is controlled

nodes.name: NLPHL advanced
nodes.title: Advanced / symptomatic NLPHL: rituximab-based therapy, then response
nodes.description: Systemic therapy incorporating an anti-CD20 antibody, with chemotherapy for higher burden; restage before surveillance.
bullets: Chemoimmunotherapy: rituximab + chemotherapy (e.g. ABVD-type or CHOP-type backbone) for symptomatic / advanced disease
Rituximab monotherapy is an option for low-burden, asymptomatic disease
Consolidative radiation to bulky sites as indicated
No dedicated NLPHL dose protocol exists in StewardMD yet - dosing is per standard references; guidance only

nodes.name: NLPHL advanced CR
nodes.title: Advanced NLPHL in complete response
nodes.description: Advanced NLPHL controlled by rituximab-based therapy.
bullets: No further therapy after a complete response; consider rituximab maintenance in selected patients
Maintain long-term follow-up given the risk of late relapse and transformation
Then survivorship surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: NLPHL advanced refractory
nodes.title: Advanced NLPHL: refractory / relapsed
nodes.description: Refractory or relapsed NLPHL needs re-biopsy and re-treatment, with attention to occult transformation.
bullets: Re-biopsy to exclude transformation to aggressive B-cell lymphoma
Re-treat with an alternate rituximab-based chemoimmunotherapy regimen
Evaluate high-risk / multiply-relapsed disease for autologous transplant per lymphoma pathways
If transformation is confirmed, treat as aggressive B-cell lymphoma

nodes.name: NLPHL transformed
nodes.title: Transformed NLPHL: treat as aggressive B-cell lymphoma
nodes.description: Histologic transformation is managed as aggressive large B-cell lymphoma with anthracycline-based chemoimmunotherapy.
bullets: Anthracycline-based chemoimmunotherapy (R-CHOP) as for aggressive large B-cell lymphoma
Consider consolidative radiation to bulky / localized sites
Evaluate high-risk / relapsed transformation for autologous transplant per lymphoma pathways
Regimen referenced below; the dose engine computes patient doses

nodes.name: Pediatric stage
nodes.title: Pediatric / adolescent cHL: risk group
nodes.description: Pediatric classical HL is treated with response-adapted multi-agent chemotherapy (interim-PET guided), minimizing radiation to reduce late effects in growing patients.

nodes.name: Pediatric low-risk
nodes.title: Pediatric low-risk cHL: abbreviated chemotherapy, then interim-PET response
nodes.description: Short-course multi-agent chemotherapy with radiation only for slow responders; adapt by interim PET.
bullets: Abbreviated response-adapted multi-agent chemotherapy (e.g. ABVE-PC backbone); minimize cumulative anthracycline and alkylator exposure
Interim FDG-PET after early cycles distinguishes rapid from slow early responders
The dose engine computes body-surface-area doses; coordinate with pediatric oncology
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Pediatric low rapid
nodes.title: Pediatric low-risk, rapid early responder: chemotherapy alone
nodes.description: A rapid early response lets radiation be omitted, sparing late effects in children.
bullets: Complete abbreviated chemotherapy alone (omit radiation) for a rapid early responder in complete response
Confirm end-of-treatment PET is negative before stopping therapy
Prioritize long-term late-effect and growth surveillance
Regimen referenced below
Then survivorship surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Pediatric low slow
nodes.title: Pediatric low-risk, slow early responder: add involved-site radiation
nodes.description: A slow early response adds low-dose involved-site radiation to the chemotherapy backbone.
bullets: Add involved-site radiation to slow-responding / initially bulky sites
Complete the planned chemotherapy course; confirm end-of-treatment response
Balance disease control against radiation late effects in a growing child
Regimen referenced below
Then survivorship surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Pediatric high-risk
nodes.title: Pediatric intermediate/high-risk cHL: intensified chemotherapy, then response
nodes.description: More cycles of multi-agent chemotherapy (brentuximab-containing in higher-risk protocols) with radiation to slow-responding / bulky sites.
bullets: Intensified response-adapted multi-agent chemotherapy (e.g. ABVE-PC, more cycles); brentuximab-containing regimens in higher-risk protocols
Interim FDG-PET guides radiation and any escalation
Prioritize fertility preservation and late-effect minimization; the dose engine computes doses
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Pediatric high CR
nodes.title: Pediatric high-risk in complete remission
nodes.description: Complete remission after intensified chemotherapy, with radiation reserved for slow responders.
bullets: Complete the planned chemotherapy; omit radiation where an early complete response allows
Record cumulative anthracycline / alkylator / brentuximab exposure for late-effect follow-up
Prioritize fertility and growth / endocrine survivorship
Regimen referenced below
Then survivorship surveillance (next step)
